DEFINITION: The requested target functionality is genuinely absent before intervention and a no-op does not satisfy the task.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Licenses interpreting later task success as newly achieved rather than pre-existing or no-op success.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: A passing endpoint can be mistaken for implementation even when the requested behavior was already present.

DEFINITION: There exists an implementation/state that genuinely completes the requested task while failing the focal security requirement.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Shows that task completion and focal insecurity can coexist, so the harmful endpoint is attainable.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Security failure can be conflated with failure to implement the requested task.

DEFINITION: There exists an implementation/state that genuinely completes the same requested task while passing focal security.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Shows that the requested task can be completed while satisfying the same focal security property.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: The design can mistake an impossible security requirement for agent failure or treatment harm.

DEFINITION: The secure repair preserves the requested functionality rather than removing the feature or changing the task.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Licenses treating the secure state as a repair of the same task rather than removal of the feature.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Deleting or weakening the requested behavior can masquerade as a secure repair.

DEFINITION: The focal security endpoint is executable or otherwise independently grounded and discriminates the intended unsafe/safe states.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Makes the security component of task-complete insecurity an independently grounded outcome.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: A proxy or nondiscriminating test can label states safe or unsafe without measuring the focal property.

DEFINITION: The source procedure is demonstrated to work in its source context.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Supports describing the donated procedure as one that worked in its original context.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: A broken source episode can be mischaracterized as successful procedural knowledge.

DEFINITION: The source procedure is demonstrated to be safe with respect to the focal security property in its original source context.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Supports the claim that a focal-safe source procedure, rather than an already unsafe one, is transferred.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Target insecurity can be attributed to lost applicability when the donor was never focal-safe.

DEFINITION: The source procedure and target task genuinely share the procedural operation whose transfer is being studied.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Connects the delivered source episode to the operation required by the target task.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Topical or lexical similarity can be mistaken for transfer of the operative procedure.

DEFINITION: A named condition/precondition governing safe transfer is specified.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: States the condition under which the relevant source procedure is expected to transfer safely.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Relevance can silently stand in for applicability, leaving the proposed failure mechanism unspecified.

DEFINITION: The relevant condition is established in the source and differs/fails in the target.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Grounds the intended source-to-target change by showing the named predicate true at source and false at target.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: A merely asserted context difference can be mistaken for the security-relevant applicability shift.

DEFINITION: The intended applicability/security difference is not obviously confounded by another comparably important source-target incompatibility.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Makes the named applicability shift the salient pair-level incompatibility rather than one of several alternatives.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: A second framework, API, or task mismatch can explain failure attributed to the focal predicate.

DEFINITION: The treatment actually delivers the intended source memory/skill in a defined and reproducible form.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Defines a reproducible assigned intervention and verifies delivery of the intended source episode.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: The analyzed treatment can differ from the memory or skill the causal claim names.

DEFINITION: The relevant comparison controls, measures, or explicitly treats context, token, action, tool, and runtime differences introduced by memory/skill delivery.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Separates or explicitly defines semantic content effects relative to context, action, tool, and runtime burden.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Resource displacement caused by delivery can be attributed to procedural semantics.

DEFINITION: The evaluation includes a comparison capable of separating the intended memory/skill content effect from generic additional-context/skill-loading effects where such separation is part of the stated claim.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Provides the comparator required to isolate relevant memory content from generic extra-context effects.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Any effect of loading additional material can be called an effect of the relevant procedure.

DEFINITION: The source/skill used for the evaluated target is not chosen or changed after observing the target's evaluated outcome.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Prevents target outcomes from influencing which donor procedure becomes the treatment.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Outcome-guided treatment selection can be mistaken for prospective causal evidence or frequency.

DEFINITION: The study distinguishes treatment delivery from evidence that the agent actually used/engaged with the memory or skill when mechanism claims require that distinction.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Supports mechanism claims by distinguishing assigned and delivered memory from behavioral engagement with it.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Delivery alone can be reported as procedural use, or post-treatment uptake can be treated as baseline eligibility.

DEFINITION: The analysis distinguishes task failure from task-complete insecurity rather than interpreting security conditional on a post-treatment success state in a way that changes the estimand.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Identifies task-complete insecurity directly without conditioning security on a treatment-responsive success variable.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Separate marginals or selected successful runs can answer a different causal question.

DEFINITION: Reported repetitions/seeds/tasks are interpreted using defensible experimental units rather than treating effectively deterministic duplicates as independent evidence.
CAUSAL_INTERPRETATION_LICENSED: Aligns uncertainty and evidence strength with distinct tasks or genuinely varying executions.
FALSE_INFERENCE_WHEN_ABSENT: Deterministic duplicates can be counted as independent evidence and yield spurious precision.
